biography: Laurent Imbert was a French missionary who joined the Paris Foreign Missions Society and worked in China before becoming vicar apostolic of Korea. He entered Korea in 1837, becoming the first bishop to reach the country. With Pierre Maubant and Jacques Chastan, he ministered to Catholic communities whose religious practice placed them at risk.

During the persecution of 1839, Imbert surrendered after learning that police had discovered his hiding place. The Korean bishops' account explains that he hoped to spare the people sheltering him. He refused demands to abandon his faith and was executed at Saenamteo. His remains were later transferred to Seoul's Myeongdong Cathedral.

biography: Pierre Maubant was a French priest of the Paris Foreign Missions Society who entered Korea in 1836. Maubant was imprisoned and executed with Imbert and Chastan at Saenamteo.

His story preserves the personal costs as well as the pastoral work of missionary life.
